title: The Gulistan
author: saadi
attributionNote: The attribution is not disputed in the scholarship this catalogue follows.
description: Saadi's book of stories, aphorisms and poems in eight chapters, moving from the conduct of kings to the morals of dervishes, contentment, silence, love, old age, education and society. A story is usually followed by a verse that turns it into a judgement, and the two are meant to be read together.
historicalContext: Written in Shiraz in 1258, after Saadi's travels through Iraq, Syria and Asia Minor. It became a school text in Persian-speaking lands and one of the first Persian works translated into European languages. Ross's English version, first published in 1823, is a selection rather than a complete rendering; the Gutenberg text also notes that some passages were omitted by its transcriber.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1823 translation by James Ross is public domain in the United States.
